tasks.title: Bicycle Turning and Inertia
tasks.transcript: We've been talking about the law of inertia: an object moving in a straight line will continue to move in a straight line unless it is acted upon by another force. When you are on a moving bicycle, inertia will keep you going in a straight line. Why don't you just turn the front wheel in the direction you want to turn? In fact, if you only turn the front wheel, you are likely to end up on the pavement. The wheel will turn, but because of inertia, your body and the rest of the bike keep moving straight ahead. How does a cyclist avoid this? The key is to lean in. Weight needs to shift in the direction of the turn so that the force of gravity can work against the force of inertia. Professional cyclists who move at high speeds lean more to keep their bicycles from sliding out of turns, but not too much. At a certain point too much lean can pull both rider and bicycle down to the ground.
